item.title: Anthropic IPO: Can Indian investors apply for Claude maker's $64 billion share sale? Check rules
item.description: Anthropic, a prominent artificial intelligence company, is planning a significant IPO to raise up to $64.4 billion. The company, founded by former OpenAI executives, aims to attract global investors, including those from India. Indian investors can participate in the offering through overseas brokerage accounts after the listing occurs. While demand for the shares appears strong, most retail investors may miss the IPO allocation.
item.dc:creator: Akash Podishetti
item.content:encoded: Anthropic, the artificial intelligence company behind the Claude chatbot, is preparing for one of the biggest stock market debuts in history, with plans to raise as much as $64.4 billion through its US initial public offering (IPO). The proposed listing has sparked interest among investors worldwide, including those in India looking to participate in the AI boom.The company has set an indicative price band of $70 to $78 per share and plans to sell 825 million shares, according to its latest filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). The offering could value Anthropic at more than $1 trillion, making it one of the world's most valuable publicly traded technology companies.However, Indian retail investors face a hurdle in securing shares at the IPO price, even though they are permitted to invest in overseas stocks.Anthropic IPO subscription and listing detailsAnthropic launched its IPO roadshow on November 10, seeking commitments from institutional investors ahead of its proposed Nasdaq listing.The company is targeting November 19 for the start of trading under the ticker symbol ANT, according to Reuters. The date remains subject to the completion of the offering and regulatory formalities.Of the 825 million shares being offered, Anthropic will issue 801.35 million fresh shares, while existing shareholders will sell 23.65 million shares.At the upper end of the price band, the offering could raise $64.4 billion.The company has also secured a separate $26 billion private placement involving major technology investors, including Google, Nvidia and AMD. Combined proceeds from the IPO and related private investments could reach $90.4 billion.Early reports suggest strong institutional interest in the offering, with MarketWatch reporting that demand has already made the issue several times oversubscribed. However, an official subscription multiple has not been publicly confirmed.Can Indian investors apply for the Anthropic IPO?Indian residents can legally invest in overseas securities under the Reserve Bank of India's Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS). The scheme allows resident individuals to remit up to $250,000 per financial year for permitted overseas transactions, including investments in foreign stocks.However, participation in a US IPO differs from applying for an Indian public issue.US IPO allocations are generally controlled by investment banks and their distribution networks, with institutional investors receiving a substantial share of the available stock.Indian investors typically do not have access to these allocations through ordinary overseas trading accounts. As a result, most retail investors in India will have to wait until Anthropic begins trading on Nasdaq before purchasing its shares.How can Indians buy Anthropic shares after listing?Once Anthropic lists in the US, eligible Indian residents can purchase its shares through overseas brokerage accounts that provide access to Nasdaq-listed stocks.Platforms offering international equity investments may allow investors to fund their accounts through the LRS route, subject to documentation, foreign exchange regulations and brokerage requirements.Investors generally need to complete know-your-customer formalities, submit the required tax documentation and remit money through an authorised banking channel.Some GIFT City-based investment platforms also provide access to US equities, depending on their product offerings and regulatory arrangements. However, investors should confirm whether their chosen platform will support trading in Anthropic shares from the listing date.Buying shares after listing also carries the risk of paying more than the IPO offer price if the stock opens at a premium.Why is the Anthropic IPO attracting attention?Founded in 2021 by former OpenAI executives, including Dario and Daniela Amodei, Anthropic has emerged as a major competitor in the global artificial intelligence industry. Its Claude AI models compete with products developed by OpenAI, Google and other technology companies.The company's revenue has grown rapidly as businesses increase spending on AI-powered software, coding tools and enterprise applications.Anthropic reported more than $16 billion in revenue during the first half of 2026, according to its IPO disclosures.However, the company remains unprofitable amid substantial spending on computing infrastructure and AI development.The proposed listing comes during a period of heightened scrutiny of AI valuations, with investors questioning whether the industry's extraordinary capital expenditure will generate sufficient returns.Disclosure: This article has been written by Podishetti Akash, who is not a SEBI-registered Research Analyst or an Investment Adviser. item.title: US stock market selloff: Four indicators suggest correction may not be over
item.description: Four key indicators suggest the US stock market correction may not be over, despite some stabilisation in technology shares. Easing investor positioning and stock correlations offer relief, but options activity and technical signals continue to point to caution.
item.dc:creator: Anupam Nagar
item.content:encoded: The recent selloff in US stocks has left investors searching for signs of a market bottom, but four key indicators suggest it may be too early to declare the correction over, according to a Reuters analysis.Technology and artificial intelligence-related stocks have fallen around 10% from their recent peaks after the Nasdaq-100 hit a record high in early October. While shares have stabilised somewhat, investor positioning, options activity and technical indicators continue to signal caution.Read more: Chinese yuan edges higher, but stronger dollar caps gains Technology positioning shows signs of easingAccording to Deutsche Bank data cited by Reuters, investors have reduced exposure to technology stocks since late September, shifting towards other sectors. The latest selloff pushed tech positioning below levels recorded during the April 2025 tariff-related market turmoil.Deutsche Bank strategist Parag Thatte said the decline appeared to be driven by investors unwinding crowded positions. He added that positioning levels could create conditions for a technology sector rebound.Stock correlations offer some reliefAnother relatively positive signal is the limited increase in expected stock correlations. Barclays strategists noted that three-month realised correlation among the 50 largest S&P 500 companies fell to a record low in late September.Although expectations for correlations increased during last week's selloff, the rise remained modest. Rocky Fishman, founder of Asym Research, said this suggested investors viewed the decline as a sector-specific correction rather than a broader economic downturn, Reuters reported.Read more: South Korean shares rise as tech stocks rebound on Wall StreetOptions activity presents a mixed pictureRetail investors had purchased call options on individual stocks in record volumes this year, helping support the AI rally. However, that trend reversed sharply last week.According to Carrick Lane data, retail call buying in AI stocks dropped significantly, contributing to the post-election selloff.The shift has reduced excessive bullish positioning, but options indicators have not weakened enough to provide a strong buying signal.Technical indicators remain cautiousTechnical signals continue to suggest that the market may not have reached its bottom. Mark Newton, head of technical strategy at Fundstrat Global Advisors, said the rebound in the Invesco QQQ ETF, which tracks the Nasdaq-100, had stalled below its downward trend line.Weak short-term momentum and the absence of a DeMark exhaustion signal suggest US stocks could remain volatile for another couple of weeks, Newton said.Overall, while reduced technology exposure and relatively stable stock correlations offer some encouragement, options positioning and technical trends suggest investors should remain cautious before calling an end to the market correction.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times.)
